akhfash:7-7.t: He said ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ إِذَا مُزِّقْتُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾: ﴿يُنْبِئُكُمْ﴾ did not operate (on إنّكم) because ﴿أَنْكُمْ﴾ is in the position of a fresh start on account of the lām, just as you say: "أَشْهَدُ إِنَّكَ لَظَرِيفٌ" (I bear witness that you are indeed witty).

akhfash:8-8.t: And He said ﴿أَفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً﴾: the alif is disjunctive because it is the alif of the interrogative; likewise the connective alif (drops) when the interrogative alif comes in upon it.

akhfash:15-15.t: And He said ﴿بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ﴾, i.e. on the basis of: "this is a good land".

akhfash:21-21.t: And He said ﴿إِلاَّ لِنَعْلَمَ﴾ as a badal (substitute), as though He said: "that trial was only so that We might know".

akhfash:23-23.t:
And He said ﴿لِمَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ﴾ because in meaning (intercession) is made only for one for whom permission has been given.
And He said ﴿قَالُواْ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾: if you wish you put it in the nominative, and if you wish you put it in the accusative.

akhfash:24-24.t: And He said ﴿وَإِنَّآ أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى﴾: this is not because it is doubt; rather, in the speech of the Arabs this means that he is the rightly guided one. A man may say to his slave "احَدُنَا ضَارِبٌ صاحِبَه" (one of us will beat the other), and there is no ambiguity for the hearer that the master is the one who beats.

akhfash:31-31.t: And He said ﴿يَرْجِعُ بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ ٱلْقَوْلَ﴾ because you say "قَدْ رَجَعْتُ إِلَيْهِ القَوْلَ" (I returned the word to him).

akhfash:33-33.t: And He said ﴿بَلْ مَكْرُ ٱلْلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ﴾, i.e. "this is the scheming of the night and the day". The night and the day do not scheme against anyone, but scheming is done in them, like His word ﴿مِّن قَرْيَتِكَ ٱلَّتِيۤ أَخْرَجَتْكَ﴾. This is from the breadth of Arabic.

akhfash:37-37.t: And He said ﴿تُقَرِّبُكُمْ عِندَنَا زُلْفَىٰ﴾ [and]. "زُلْفى" here is a noun of the maṣdar (verbal noun), as though He meant: "by that which brings you near to Us with a bringing-near (إِزْلافا)".

akhfash:45-45.t: And He said ﴿مِعْشَارَ مَآ آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾, i.e. a tenth of it. They do not say this (pattern) for anything other than the tenth.

daas-irab:1-2.t: ﴿الْحَمْدُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative noun, naʿt (adjective) of الله. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿ما﴾ relative, postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila. ﴿وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿الْحَمْدُ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فِي الْآخِرَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and هو is mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْحَكِيمُ﴾ first khabar. ﴿الْخَبِيرُ﴾ second khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَلِجُ﴾ the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يلج. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and ما is relative, conjoined to what precedes. ﴿يَخْرُجُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يخرج. ﴿وَما يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿الرَّحِيمُ الْغَفُورُ﴾ two predicates of the mubtadaʾ.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لا تَأْتِينَا﴾ لا is negative, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿السَّاعَةُ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of reply. ﴿وَرَبِّي﴾ the wāw is a preposition and a particle of oath; ربي is genitive (majrūr) and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb أقسم (I swear). ﴿لَتَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), the kāf is its mafʿūl bihi, and the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural. ﴿عالِمِ﴾ naʿt (adjective) of ربّ. ﴿الْغَيْبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. It was also read «عالمُ» with the ḍamma, in which case it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لا يَعْزُبُ﴾ لا is negative, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يعزب. ﴿مِثْقالُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿ذَرَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَلا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative. ﴿أَصْغَرُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ ذلِكَ﴾ the demonstrative is in the position of the genitive, and the two are attached to the khabar. ﴿وَلا أَكْبَرُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿فِي كِتابٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ naʿt.

daas-irab:4-6.t: ﴿لِيَجْزِيَ﴾ the lām is the lām of causation (lām al-taʿlīl), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of causation; the lām and what follows it are attached to (mutaʿalliq) لتأتينّكم; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to آمنوا. ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ the demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مَغْفِرَةٌ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the khabar of أولئك. ﴿وَرِزْقٌ﴾ conjoined. ﴿كَرِيمٌ﴾ naʿt (adjective). ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ its i'rab has been given; the clause is the khabar of الذين. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿سَعَوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِي آياتِنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to سعوا, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مُعاجِزِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the khabar of أولئك. ﴿مِنْ رِجْزٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ naʿt. ﴿وَيَرَى﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and its mafʿūl bihi [Translator's note: so in the source; أُوتوا is passive and its wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil]; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ the relative noun, first mafʿūl bihi of يرى, and الحق is its second object, because the cognitive يرى (of the heart) takes two objects in the accusative. ﴿أُنْزِلَ﴾ a passive past verb; the nāʾib fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أنزل. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أنزل. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position. ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ the second object of يرى. ﴿وَيَهْدِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness; the fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلى صِراطِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them. ﴿الْعَزِيزِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْحَمِيدِ﴾ naʿt.

daas-irab:7-8.t: ﴿وَقالَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil (agent) of قال. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿هَلْ﴾ an interrogative particle. ﴿نَدُلُّكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb; the kāf is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿عَلى رَجُلٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ندلّكم. ﴿يُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of رجل. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb for future time, putting its condition in the genitive and made accusative by its apodosis. ﴿مُزِّقْتُمْ﴾ a passive past verb, and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كُلَّ﴾ a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq). ﴿مُمَزَّقٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِنَّكُمْ﴾ إنّ and its noun. ﴿لَفِي خَلْقٍ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of إنّ. ﴿جَدِيدٍ﴾ naʿt of خلق; the clause stands in place of the two objects of ينبّئكم. ﴿أَفْتَرى﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to افترى. ﴿الكذب﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿جِنَّةٌ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is conjoined. ﴿بَلِ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يؤمنون. ﴿فِي الْعَذابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿وَالضَّلالِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to في العذاب. ﴿الْبَعِيدِ﴾ naʿt.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿أَفَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لم is a particle of negation, jussive and inversion (to the past) [Translator's note: the source has «وحزم», a misprint for «وجزم» (jussive)]. ﴿يَرَوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the elision of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿إِلى ما﴾ ما is relative; the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يروا. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَما خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; خلفهم is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السماء. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a jussive conditional particle. ﴿نَشَأْ﴾ the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive. ﴿نَخْسِفْ﴾ the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿بِهِمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to نخسف. ﴿الْأَرْضِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿نُسْقِطْ﴾ conjoined to نخسف, jussive like it. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to نسقط. ﴿كِسَفاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of كسفا; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters) [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic text here is إِنَّ]. ﴿فِي ذلِكَ﴾ the demonstrative is genitive by في, and the two are attached to a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿لَآيَةً﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and آية is the noun of إنّ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt of آية. ﴿عَبْدٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مُنِيبٍ﴾ naʿt of عبد.

daas-irab:10-11.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿آتَيْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿داوُدَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنَّا﴾ من and نا, attached to (mutaʿalliq) آتينا. ﴿فَضْلًا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi of آتينا; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يا﴾ a vocative particle. ﴿جِبالُ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative by the vocative; the vocative clause is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "قلنا" (We said). ﴿أَوِّبِي﴾ an imperative verb indeclinable on the elision of the nūn, and the yāʾ is the fāʿil. ﴿مَعَهُ﴾ an adverb of place, attached to أوّبي, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالطَّيْرَ﴾ conjoined to the position of جبال; it was also read in the nominative, conjoined to the form. ﴿وَأَلَنَّا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ألنّا. ﴿الْحَدِيدَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنِ﴾ explicative (mufassira). ﴿اعْمَلْ سابِغاتٍ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); سابغات is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl bihi, its implied form being "دروعا سابغات" (ample coats of mail); the clause is explicative, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَقَدِّرْ﴾ an imperative verb. ﴿فِي السَّرْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قدّر; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَاعْمَلُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿صالِحاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ إنّ and its noun; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to بصير. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بَصِيرٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَلِسُلَيْمانَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "سخّرنا" (We subjected). ﴿الرِّيحَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the omitted verb سخّرنا; the clause is resumptive. ﴿غُدُوُّها شَهْرٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَرَواحُها شَهْرٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَسَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them. ﴿عَيْنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْقِطْرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَمِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted verb سخّرنا. ﴿مِنَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the omitted verb سخّرنا [Translator's note: so vocalized in the source; the Quranic word is مَنْ]. ﴿يَعْمَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ attached to the verb before them. ﴿بِإِذْنِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿رَبِّهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَمِنَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and مَن is conditional, mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: so vocalized in the source; the Quranic word is وَمَنْ]. ﴿يَزِغْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its fāʿil is latent. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿عَنْ أَمْرِنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿نُذِقْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); its fāʿil is latent and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl bihi; the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ عَذابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them. ﴿السَّعِيرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:13-14.t: ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a badal (substitute) of the earlier verb يعمل. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْ مَحارِيبَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَتَماثِيلَ وَجِفانٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to محاريب. ﴿كَالْجَوابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of جفان. A جفنة is what food is placed in, and الجوابي are wide ones, holding food for a thousand people. ﴿وَقُدُورٍ﴾ conjoined. ﴿راسِياتٍ﴾ naʿt. ﴿اعْمَلُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿آلَ﴾ the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle, the implied form being «يا آل». ﴿داوُدَ﴾ the one addressed [Translator's note: so in the source; داود is muḍāf ilayhi of آل]. ﴿شُكْراً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a naʿt of a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَقَلِيلٌ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْ عِبادِيَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الشَّكُورُ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive and لمّا is adverbial. ﴿قَضَيْنا عَلَيْهِ الْمَوْتَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿دَلَّهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of لمّا. ﴿عَلى مَوْتِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿دَابَّةُ﴾ fāʿil of دلّهم. ﴿الْأَرْضِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿تَأْكُلُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿مِنْسَأَتَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. The منسأة is the staff with which animals are driven. ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ a conjunction, and لمّا is an adverb of time, a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿خَرَّ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿تَبَيَّنَتِ الْجِنُّ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened from أنّ, its noun omitted. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿كانُوا﴾ كان and its noun; the clause is the khabar of أنْ. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the clause is the khabar of كان. ﴿الْغَيْبَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿لَبِثُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of the non-jussive لو. ﴿فِي الْعَذابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to لبثوا. ﴿الْمُهِينِ﴾ naʿt. This verse is a great proof that none knows the Unseen but Allah, and in it is a refutation of the charlatans and soothsayers who claim to know the Unseen while they seek the help of devils; the devils are veiled from the Unseen, for had they known of the death of Solomon, peace be upon him, they would not have continued in his service.

daas-irab:15-16.t: ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لِسَبَإٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿فِي مَسْكَنِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿آيَةٌ﴾ the noun of كان; the clause is resumptive. ﴿جَنَّتانِ﴾ khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "الآية جنتان" (the sign is two gardens), nominative (marfūʿ) with the alif because it is a dual. ﴿عَنْ يَمِينٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of جنتان. ﴿وَشِمالٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿كُلُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ رِزْقِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿رَبِّكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَاشْكُرُوا﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to اشكروا. ﴿بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ﴾ بلدة is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي" (it), and طيبة is a naʿt. ﴿وَرَبٌّ غَفُورٌ﴾ conjoined to بلدة طيبة. ﴿فَأَعْرَضُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَأَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سَيْلَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أرسلنا; the clause is conjoined. ﴿الْعَرِمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَبَدَّلْناهُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them. ﴿جَنَّتَيْنِ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi of بدّل, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a dual. ﴿ذَواتَيْ﴾ naʿt of جنتين, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is a dual [Translator's note: so in the source; as a naʿt of the accusative جنتين it is accusative with the yāʾ]. ﴿أُكُلٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿خَمْطٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. الخمط is that which is intensely bitter. ﴿وَأَثْلٍ﴾ conjoined; it is a tree without fruit that grows in the wilderness. ﴿وَشَيْءٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْ سِدْرٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of شيء. ﴿قَلِيلٍ﴾ naʿt of شيء. The lote-tree (السدر) has no fruit.

daas-irab:17-19.t: ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ the demonstrative, second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of جزيناهم; the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. ﴿جَزَيْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَهَلْ﴾ an interrogative particle. ﴿نُجازِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿الْكَفُورَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ in the place of the second object of جعل, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَبَيْنَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to بينهم. ﴿الْقُرَى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ the relative noun, naʿt (adjective) of القرى. ﴿بارَكْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them. ﴿قُرىً﴾ first object of جعلنا. ﴿ظاهِرَةً﴾ naʿt of قرى; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَقَدَّرْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فِيها﴾ attached to the verb before them. ﴿السَّيْرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿سِيرُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فِيها﴾ attached to the verb before them. ﴿لَيالِيَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿وَأَيَّاماً﴾ conjoined to ليالي. ﴿آمِنِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿فَقالُوا﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿باعِدْ﴾ a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place, attached to the verb before it. ﴿أَسْفارِنا﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَظَلَمُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿أَحادِيثَ﴾ second object of جعلنا. ﴿وَمَزَّقْناهُمْ﴾ the clause is conjoined, like the preceding one. ﴿كُلَّ﴾ a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq). ﴿مُمَزَّقٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters). ﴿فِي ذلِكَ﴾ the demonstrative is genitive by في, and the two are attached to the omitted fronted khabar (predicate); the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. ﴿لَآياتٍ﴾ the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and آيات is the postponed noun of إنّ, accusative with the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to آيات. ﴿صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ﴾ two adjectives (naʿt).

daas-irab:20-22.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ its i'rab has been given. ﴿صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿ظَنَّهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَاتَّبَعُوهُ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿فَرِيقاً﴾ excepted (mustathnā) by إلا, accusative (manṣūb). ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of فريقا. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿سُلْطانٍ﴾ a noun genitive in form and nominative in position, the noun of كان; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ﴾ the lām is for causation, and an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of causation; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنْ﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi of نعلم [Translator's note: so vocalized in the source; the Quranic word is مَنْ]. ﴿يُؤْمِنُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يؤمن. ﴿مِمَّنْ﴾ composed of two words, the preposition مِن and the relative noun مَن; the two are attached to an omitted khabar. ﴿هُوَ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿فِي شَكٍّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the fronted khabar [Translator's note: so in the source, which also attaches مِمَّن to an omitted khabar above; on the usual analysis هو is the mubtadaʾ and في شك is attached to its khabar]. ﴿وَرَبُّكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is حفيظ, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to حفيظ. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿حَفِيظٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿قُلِ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿ادْعُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿زَعَمْتُمْ﴾ the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the naʿt of the omitted second object of زعمتم. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَمْلِكُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿مِثْقالَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ذَرَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يملكون. ﴿وَلا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿فِيهِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant preposition. ﴿شِرْكٍ﴾ a noun genitive in form and nominative in position, mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant preposition. ﴿ظَهِيرٍ﴾ a noun genitive in form and nominative in position, postponed mubtadaʾ.

daas-irab:23-24.t: ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative. ﴿تَنْفَعُ الشَّفاعَةُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined. ﴿عِنْدَهُ﴾ an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before it, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ the lām is a preposition and مَن is a relative noun; the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَذِنَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أذن. It was also read «أُذِنَ» in the passive. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit and a preposition. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb for future time, putting its condition in the genitive and made accusative by its apodosis. ﴿فُزِّعَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). It was also read in the active voice. ﴿قالُوا﴾ the clause is the apodosis of إذا, with no grammatical position. ﴿ماذا﴾ ما is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and ذا is a relative noun, khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قالَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ naʿt (adjective) of a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "قال القول الحق" (He said the true word). ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its two predicates; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَرْزُقُكُمْ﴾ the clause is the khabar. ﴿مِنَ السَّماواتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السموات. ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being "الله يرزقنا" (Allah provides for us); the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿وَإِنَّا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and إنّ and its noun; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ﴾ أو is a conjunction and إياكم is a pronoun conjoined to the noun of إنّا, which is نا. ﴿لَعَلى هُدىً﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar of إنّا, its implied form being "كائنون لعلى هدى" (are upon guidance); the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ conjoined to لعلى هدى. ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ naʿt of ضلال.

daas-irab:25-27.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿تُسْئَلُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿عَمَّا﴾ عن is a preposition and ما is relative; the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿أَجْرَمْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَلا نُسْئَلُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, لا is negative, and a passive imperfect verb whose nāʾib fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَمَّا﴾ attached to نسأل; the clause is conjoined. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَجْمَعُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿بَيْنَنا﴾ an adverb of place, attached to the verb before it, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿رَبُّنا﴾ fāʿil of يجمع, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَفْتَحُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بَيْنَنا﴾ an adverb, attached to the verb before it, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يفتح. ﴿وَهُوَ الْفَتَّاحُ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its two predicates; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَرُونِيَ﴾ an imperative verb; the wāw is its fāʿil, and the nūn is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) — it is so called because it protects the verb from the kasra — and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَلْحَقْتُمْ﴾ a past verb; the tāʾ is its fāʿil and the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them. ﴿شُرَكاءَ﴾ third mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Divine Name, khabar (predicate), nominative with the ḍamma. ﴿الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ two adjectives (naʿt).

daas-irab:28-31.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is resumptive and ما is negative. ﴿أَرْسَلْناكَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿كَافَّةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb). ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كافة. ﴿بَشِيراً﴾ ḥāl, accusative. ﴿وَنَذِيراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to بشيرا. ﴿وَلكِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters). ﴿أَكْثَرَ﴾ the noun of لكنّ. ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of لكنّ, in the position of the nominative. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مَتى﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb, attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿هذَا﴾ a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْوَعْدُ﴾ badal (substitute) of the demonstrative. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a jussive conditional particle. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ كان and its noun. ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾ the khabar of كان, accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The apodosis of the condition is omitted because what precedes indicates it. ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿مِيعادُ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَوْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿لا تَسْتَأْخِرُونَ﴾ لا is negative, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of يوم. ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them. ﴿ساعَةً﴾ an adverb of time, attached to the verb before it. ﴿وَلا تَسْتَقْدِمُونَ﴾ the clause is conjoined to the preceding one, and its i'rab is like its i'rab. ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb, and the relative noun is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لَنْ﴾ a subjunctive particle (nāṣiba). ﴿نُؤْمِنَ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِهذَا﴾ the demonstrative is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the two are attached to the verb; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿الْقُرْآنِ﴾ badal of هذا. ﴿وَلا بِالَّذِي﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb, attached to an omitted ṣila. ﴿يَدَيْهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is a dual, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿تَرى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِذِ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿مَوْقُوفُونَ﴾ khabar, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَرْجِعُ بَعْضُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلى بَعْضٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them. ﴿الْقَوْلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is explicative. ﴿اسْتُضْعِفُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun is genitive by the lām, and the two are attached to يقول. ﴿اسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لَوْلا﴾ a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ whose khabar is necessarily omitted. ﴿لَكُنَّا﴾ the lām is connective for the apodosis, and كان and its noun. ﴿مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ the khabar of كنّا; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.

daas-irab:32-33.t:
﴿قالَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb, and الذين is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿اسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) قال. ﴿اسْتُضْعِفُوا﴾ a passive past verb and nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَنَحْنُ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation and نحن is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿صَدَدْناكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿عَنِ الْهُدى﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them. ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ an adverb, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb in construct with an adverb. ﴿جاءَكُمْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the kāf is its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿كُنْتُمْ مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ كان, its noun and its khabar. ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ see the i'rab of the previous verse. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression and conjunction. ﴿مَكْرُ﴾ mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted. ﴿اللَّيْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالنَّهارِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الليل; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb, attached to مكر. ﴿تَأْمُرُونَنا﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a subjunctive particle (nāṣiba). ﴿نَكْفُرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; أن نكفر is construed as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), attached to تأمروننا. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ the Divine Name is genitive by the bāʾ, and the two are attached to نكفر. ﴿وَنَجْعَلَ﴾ conjoined to نكفر. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿أَنْداداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi of نجعل. ﴿وَأَسَرُّوا النَّدامَةَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ an adverb of time, called «لمّا» of time (al-ḥīniyya). ﴿رَأَوُا﴾ a past verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا الْأَغْلالَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فِي أَعْناقِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جعلنا, and they stand in the place of the second object. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. ﴿هَلْ﴾ an interrogative particle. ﴿يُجْزَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ما﴾
a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the verb يجزون. ﴿كانُوا﴾ كان, and the wāw is in the position of the nominative as the noun of كان; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كان.

daas-irab:34-36.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is resumptive and ما is negative. ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فِي قَرْيَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿نَذِيرٍ﴾ a noun genitive in form and accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿قالَ مُتْرَفُوها﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِنَّا﴾ إنّ and its noun; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بِما﴾ ما is a relative noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the khabar (predicate) after them. ﴿أُرْسِلْتُمْ﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; أرسلتم is a passive past verb, the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أرسلتم. ﴿كافِرُونَ﴾ the khabar of إنّا, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿نَحْنُ أَكْثَرُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar; the clause is the object of the saying, in the position of the accusative. ﴿أَمْوالًا﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿وَأَوْلاداً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ما operates like ليس. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ a pronoun in the position of the nominative as the noun of ما; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِمُعَذَّبِينَ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and معذَّبين is accusative in position as the khabar of ما. ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ رَبِّي﴾ إنّ and its noun, accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿يَبْسُطُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿الرِّزْقَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of إنّ, and its position is the nominative. ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ مَن is the relative noun; the two are attached to يبسط. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَيَقْدِرُ﴾ the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلكِنَّ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of the ḥāl, and لكنّ is a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); it enters upon the nominal sentence, puts the first part in the accusative, which is called its noun, and the second in the nominative, which is called its khabar. ﴿أَكْثَرَ﴾ the noun of لكنّ. ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of لكنّ.

daas-irab:37-38.t: ﴿وَما﴾ ما is negative, operating like ليس. ﴿أَمْوالُكُمْ﴾ the nominative noun of ما, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَلا أَوْلادُكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes. ﴿بِالَّتِي﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and the relative noun is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar (predicate) of ما; the clause is conjoined. ﴿تُقَرِّبُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the kāf is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿عِنْدَنا﴾ an adverb of place, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿زُلْفى﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) according to the meaning, i.e., «تقرّبكم قربى» (bring you near a nearness). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception in the sense of «لكن» (but). ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, excepted (mustathnā) by إلا. ﴿آمَنَ﴾ the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, its fāʿil latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾ connective for the apodosis, because the relative noun has the sense of a condition; أولاء is mubtadaʾ (subject), indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra in the position of the nominative, and the kāf is for address. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the fronted khabar. ﴿جَزاءُ﴾ mubtadaʾ; the clause is the khabar of أولئك. ﴿الضِّعْفِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جزاء. ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾ a past verb [and] its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فِي الْغُرُفاتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar. ﴿آمِنُونَ﴾ khabar, nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and the relative noun is mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يَسْعَوْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. And the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿فِي آياتِنا﴾ are attached to يسعون, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مُعاجِزِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي الْعَذابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar after them. ﴿مُحْضَرُونَ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural.

daas-irab:39-39.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ رَبِّي﴾ إنّ and its noun, and the bāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) [Translator's note: so in the source, a misprint for the yāʾ]; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. ﴿لِمَنْ يَشاءُ مِنْ عِبادِهِ وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ﴾ see verse 16 [Translator's note: so in the source; the parallel analysis is at verse 36]. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is a jussive conditional noun that puts two verbs in the jussive, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of أنفقتم. ﴿أَنْفَقْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَهُوَ﴾ the fāʾ is connective for the apodosis, and هو is mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿يُخْلِفُهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿وَهُوَ خَيْرُ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿الرَّازِقِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:40-41.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَحْشُرُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَقُولُ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿لِلْمَلائِكَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يقول. ﴿أَهؤُلاءِ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, and أولاء is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿إِيَّاكُمْ﴾ an accusative pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the verb يعبدون, placed before it. ﴿كانُوا﴾ كان and its noun; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of هؤلاء. ﴿يَعْبُدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا. ﴿قالُوا﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿سُبْحانَكَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَنْتَ وَلِيُّنا﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause together with what precedes it is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿كانُوا﴾ كان and its noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَعْبُدُونَ الْجِنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of كانوا. ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what comes after them. ﴿مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is a badal (substitute) of the clause before it.

daas-irab:42-43.t: ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb after it. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَمْلِكُ بَعْضُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِبَعْضٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to نفعا. ﴿نَفْعاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَلا ضَرًّا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; the clause is in construct with يوم. ﴿وَنَقُولُ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun is genitive by the lām, and the two are attached to تقول [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb is نقول]. ﴿ظَلَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿ذُوقُوا عَذابَ﴾ an imperative verb; the wāw is its fāʿil and عذاب its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿النَّارِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ a relative noun, naʿt (adjective). ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ كان and its noun; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb after them. ﴿تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم. ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and إذا is an adverb containing the sense of a condition. ﴿تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility; آياتنا is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and نا is muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تتلى; the clause is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَيِّناتٍ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿قالُوا﴾ the clause is the apodosis of إذا, with no grammatical position. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿هذا﴾ the demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿رَجُلٌ﴾ the khabar of هذا. ﴿يُرِيدُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَنْ يَصُدَّكُمْ﴾ أن and the imperfect verb made accusative by it are construed as a maṣdar (verbal noun), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of يريد. ﴿عَمَّا﴾ composed of the preposition عن and the relative ما; the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is omitted; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يَعْبُدُ آباؤُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كان. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿هذا﴾ a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿إِفْكٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿مُفْتَرىً﴾ naʿt, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility. ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb, and the relative noun is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لِلْحَقِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قال. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ the temporal (ḥīniyya) لمّا, an adverb of time. ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is latent; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَنْ﴾ negative [Translator's note: so vocalized in the source; the Quranic word is the negative إِنْ]. ﴿هذا﴾ the demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿سِحْرٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ its naʿt; the clause is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:44-45.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. ﴿آتَيْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ كُتُبٍ﴾ كتب is a noun genitive in form, in the position of the accusative as the second object of آتيناهم. ﴿يَدْرُسُونَها﴾ an imperfect verb, fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of كتب. ﴿وَما أَرْسَلْنا﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أرسلنا. ﴿قَبْلَكَ﴾ an adverb of time, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿نَذِيرٍ﴾ a noun genitive in form and accusative in position, second mafʿūl bihi of أرسلنا [Translator's note: so in the source; أرسل takes a single object here]. ﴿وَكَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, and the relative noun is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ما is negative. ﴿بَلَغُوا مِعْشارَ﴾ a past verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil and معشار is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ما﴾ relative, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿آتَيْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فَكَذَّبُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿رُسُلِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction and كيف is interrogative, in the position of the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان. ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿نَكِيرِ﴾ the nominative noun of كان; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:46-48.t:
﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿أَعِظُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the kāf is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بِواحِدَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a subjunctive particle (nāṣiba). ﴿تَقُومُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by the elision of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; أن and what follows it are construed as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive as badal (substitute) of واحدة. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the Divine Name is genitive by the lām, and the two are attached to تقوموا. ﴿مَثْنى﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif owing to impossibility. ﴿وَفُرادى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to مثنى. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿تَتَفَكَّرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb conjoined to تقوموا, accusative like it by the elision of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿بِصاحِبِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and جنّة is its mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿جِنَّةٍ﴾ a noun genitive in form and nominative in position, postponed mubtadaʾ. الجِنّة is madness. The clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنْ﴾ negative [Translator's note: so vocalized in the source; the Quranic word is the negative إِنْ]. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿نَذِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of هو. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿يَدَيْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the yāʾ because it is a dual; the nūn was elided because of the construct. ﴿عَذابٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿شَدِيدٍ﴾ naʿt (adjective) of عذاب. ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾
a jussive conditional noun, in the position of the accusative, and second object of سألتكم. ﴿سَأَلْتُكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the kāf is its mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْ أَجْرٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿فَهُوَ لَكُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and a mubtadaʾ; لكم is attached to the implied, omitted khabar; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿إِنْ أَجْرِيَ﴾ إن is negative; أجري is mubtadaʾ and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to شهيد. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿شَهِيدٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ رَبِّي﴾ إنّ and its noun, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَقْذِفُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يقذف. ﴿عَلَّامُ﴾ second khabar of إنّ. ﴿الْغُيُوبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:49-51.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿جاءَ الْحَقُّ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. ﴿يُبْدِئُ الْباطِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَما يُعِيدُ﴾ its i'rab is like the i'rab of what precedes it. ﴿قُلْ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a jussive conditional particle that puts two verbs in the jussive; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿ضَلَلْتُ﴾ a past verb, and the tāʾ is its fāʿil; the clause of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿فَإِنَّما﴾ the fāʾ is connective for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and إنما is restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿أَضِلُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿عَلى نَفْسِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أضلّ. ﴿وَإِنِ اهْتَدَيْتُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to إن ضللت. ﴿فَبِما﴾ the fāʾ is connective for the apodosis, the yāʾ is a preposition [Translator's note: so in the source, a misprint for the bāʾ], and ما is relative; the two are attached to يوحى. ﴿يُوحِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يوحي. ﴿رَبِّي﴾ fāʿil, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ قَرِيبٌ﴾ إنّ, the hāʾ is its noun, and سميع قريب are its two predicates; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and لو is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿تَرى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿فَزِعُوا﴾ a past verb, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive and لا is the lā of generic negation. ﴿فَوْتَ﴾ the noun of the lā of generic negation, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; its khabar (predicate) is omitted. ﴿وَأُخِذُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ مَكانٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أخذوا. ﴿قَرِيبٍ﴾ naʿt (adjective) of مكان.

daas-irab:52-54.t: ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿آمَنَّا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿وَأَنَّى﴾ the wāw is the wāw of the ḥāl, and أنّى is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿التَّناوُشُ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). التناوش is reaching for faith on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿مِنْ مَكانٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to التناوش. ﴿بَعِيدٍ﴾ naʿt (adjective) of مكان. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of the ḥāl and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَيَقْذِفُونَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يقذفون. ﴿مِنْ مَكانٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يقذفون. ﴿بَعِيدٍ﴾ naʿt of مكان. ﴿وَحِيلَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb whose nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَبَيْنَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the construct. ﴿يَشْتَهُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿كَما﴾ the kāf is a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and ما is relative. ﴿فُعِلَ﴾ a passive past verb whose fāʿil is latent [Translator's note: so in the source; with a passive verb it is the nāʾib fāʿil]; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِأَشْياعِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ إنّ, and the hāʾ is in the position of the accusative as its noun; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya). ﴿كانُوا﴾ كان, and the wāw is in the position of the nominative as its noun; the clause is the khabar of إنّ. ﴿فِي شَكٍّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of كانوا. ﴿مُرِيبٍ﴾ naʿt of شك.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلاَّمِ الغَيْبِ﴾: he said: I saw it in the copy of the Qurʾān of ʿAbdullāh as (عَلاَّمِ), according to the reading of his companions. ʿĀṣim read it (عَالِم الغَيْب) in the genitive, as a description of Allah. The people of the Ḥijāz read (عالِمُ الغَيْبِ) in the nominative as a fresh start (iʾtināf), since words intervene between the two; as He said ﴿رَبِّ السمواتِ والأرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُما الرحمنُ﴾ and made it nominative, while the noun before it is genitive. All are correct.
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَعْزُبُ عَنْهُ﴾ and ﴿يَعْزِبُ﴾ are two dialectal forms, and both have been read. The kasra is dearer to me.

farraa:5-5.t: His saying ﴿عَذَابٌ مِّن رِّجْزٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾: the readers read it in the genitive. Had it been made a naʿt (adjective) of العذاب and put in the nominative, it would have been permissible; as the readers read ﴿عَالِيَهُمْ ثِيَابُ سُنْدُسٍ خُضْرٍ﴾ and ﴿خُضْرٌ﴾, and read ﴿فى لَوْح محفوظٍ﴾ [qualifying] the Tablet, and ﴿محفوظٌ﴾ [qualifying] the Qurʾān. All are correct.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ﴾: (يرى) is in the position of an accusative [subjunctive]. Its meaning is: that He may recompense those … and that those … may see (he recited the verse). If you wish, you begin it afresh and make it nominative [indicative], and the meaning is a fresh start, not referred back to كَيْ.
His saying ﴿وَيَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْعِلْمَ﴾: you make (العلم) accusative because it comes out of [a verb] whose agent is not named, and you make ﴿الذينَ﴾ nominative through (يرى). Its meaning is only: and those who were given the Torah see — ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām and his companions among the Muslims of the People of the Book. His saying ﴿هُوَ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾: (هو) is a ʿimād (support pronoun) [Translator's note: the Kufan term for what the Basrans call the ḍamīr al-faṣl, the separating pronoun] for الذى. You make ﴿الحقَّ﴾ accusative when you make it a ʿimād. Had you made ﴿الحقّ﴾ nominative, making (هو) a noun [i.e. mubtadaʾ (subject)], it would have been correct. Al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
ليت الشباب هو الرجِيعُ عَلَى الفتى * والشيبَ كان هو البَدِئ الأوّلُ
(Would that youth were what returns to a young man, and grey hair had been what came first.)
He used the nominative with (كان) and the accusative with (ليت). The accusative is permissible with every [noun having] alif and lām, and with "afʿal minka" (more … than you) and its kind. It is also permissible with nouns that are by their nature definite [i.e. proper names], except that the nominative is more common with [such] names. You say كان عبدُالله هو أخوك (ʿAbdullāh was your brother) more often than كان عبدالله هو أخاك. Al-Farrāʾ said: he allows this, and no other grammarian allows it. [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently a transmitter's remark that al-Farrāʾ alone allows the accusative here.] And [in] كان أبو محمّد هو زيدٌ, the speech of the Arabs is the nominative. They preferred the nominative with names only because the alif and lām were introduced / 151 a [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] as a support for that in which they occur, just as (هو) was introduced as a support for the noun before it. So when they do not find alif and lām in the noun after it, they choose the nominative and treat it like the indefinite; for they say nothing but كانَ عبدالله هو قائم. They allowed the accusative only in أفضل منك (better than you) and its kind, because there is no way to introduce the alif and lām into it, so they allowed their meaning to take effect even though they do not appear, since it is not possible to make them appear. As for قائم, you are able to put the alif and lām on it, so when you do not bring them, they make هو before it a noun, not a ʿimād, since the verbal word [i.e. the participle] has not been supported with alif and lām. The poet said:
أجِدَّك لَنْ تزال نجِىَّ هَمٍّ * تبيتُ الليلَ أنت له ضجيع
(Truly, will you never cease to be the confidant of care, spending the night as its bedfellow?)

farraa:7-8.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ هَلْ نَدُلُّكُمْ﴾: the Arabs assimilate the lām into the nūn when the lām is quiescent and the nūn is vowelled. That is because it is close to it in point of articulation. It is frequent in recitation. They do not do that with a lām that is sometimes vowelled, such as ادخل and قل, because (قل) [i.e. the verb يقول] used to take the nominative and the accusative, and the jussive enters upon it; whereas هل, بل and أَجَلْ are always quiescent (majzūm), so when they are assimilated they are likened to His saying ﴿النار﴾, when the lām of النار is assimilated into its nūn. Likewise His saying ﴿فَهَلْ تَرَى لَهُمْ مِنْ بَاقِيَةٍ﴾: you assimilate the lām into the tāʾ in بل, هل and أَجَلْ, and you do not assimilate in a lām that is sometimes vowelled. Pronouncing them clearly (iẓhār) is permissible, because the lām is not joined to what follows it as the lām of النار and the like is joined. I have come to choose ﴿هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ﴾ and ﴿بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ﴾ with clear pronunciation only because the recitation of the non-native-born (muwalladūn) is something crafted; they did not take it from the instinct of the Bedouin, they took it by craft. For the Bedouin it is permissible, given the light and heavy speech that runs on his tongue. If I were to make recitation conform by analogy to what is light on the tongues of the Arabs, so that they lighten or assimilate, I would lighten His saying ﴿قُلْ أَىُّ شَىْءٍ أَكْبَرُ شَهَادَةً﴾ and say أَيْشٍ أكبرُ شهادة, which is the speech of the Arabs. But recitation is not on that basis [Translator's note: the source has فيلس, apparently for فليس]; recitation is on fullness and giving each sound its due; and because the particle is not joined like the alif and lām: do you not see that you do not pause on the alif and lām [apart] from the word in which they are? For that reason I did not pronounce the lām clearly before the tāʾ and the like. [Translator's note: so in the source; this appears to contradict his stated preference for clear pronunciation just above.] Likewise His saying ﴿اتَّخَذْتُم﴾ and ﴿عُذْتُ بِرَبِّى وَرَبِّكُمْ﴾: you may pronounce clearly or assimilate. Assimilation is dearer to me, because it is joined to a letter before which one cannot pause. As for His saying ﴿بَلْ رَانَ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾, the lām enters very strongly into the rāʾ, and it is heavy on the tongue to pronounce it clearly, so it is assimilated. Do likewise with all assimilation: whatever is heavy on the tongue to pronounce clearly, assimilate; and whatever is easy for you to pronounce clearly, pronounce clearly and do not assimilate.

His saying: ﴿لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾ ﴿أَفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً﴾: this alif is interrogative, so it is a disjunctive alif (maqṭūʿa) both in pause and in continuation, because it is the alif of interrogation; the alif after it fell away because it is light and redundant, falling away in connected speech. Likewise His saying ﴿سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ﴾ and His saying ﴿أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ﴾ — Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm recited the verse — and His saying ﴿أَصْطَفَى البَنَاتِ عَلَى البَنِينَ﴾. It is not permissible to give the alif a kasra here, because the interrogation would be lost. If you say: why, when two alifs come together, did you not lengthen, as He said ﴿آلذكرين﴾ and ﴿آلآنَ﴾? I say: the alif was lengthened in الآن and the like only because its alif had a fatḥa; had you dropped it, you would find no / 151 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] difference between interrogative and declarative, so the lengthening of the alif was made a distinction between interrogative and declarative. In His saying ﴿أَفْتَرَىٰ﴾ its alif had a kasra and the interrogative alif a fatḥa, so they were distinct and had no need to lengthen the alif.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ إِلَىٰ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾: He says: do they not know that wherever they are, they see before them of the earth and the sky the like of what is behind them, and that they cannot get out of them? So how do they feel safe from Our making the earth swallow them, or dropping upon them a punishment from the sky?

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰجِبَالُ أَوِّبِي مَعَهُ وَٱلطَّيْرَ﴾: the readers who are known agree on doubling ﴿أَوِّبِي﴾, and its meaning is: glorify [Allah]. Some read (أُوبِى مَعَهُ), from آب يؤوب, i.e. go about with him. ﴿وَٱلطَّيْرَ﴾ is accusative in two ways. One is that you make it accusative by the verb, through His saying ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ مِنَّا فَضْلاً﴾: and We subjected the birds to him. It is then like your saying أطعمته طعاماً وماء (I fed him food and water), meaning: and I gave him water to drink; that is permissible. The other way is by the vocative, because when you say يا عمرو والصَلْت أقبِلا (O ʿAmr and al-Ṣalt, come forward), you make الصلت accusative, because it can only be called with يا أيُّها, so when that is missing, it is as though diverted from its proper path, and it is made accusative. It may also be nominative by following what precedes it. And it may be nominative on [the meaning]: glorify, you and the birds. One of the Arabs recited to me, regarding the vocative when it is made accusative for lack of يا أيُّها:
أَلا يَا عَمْرُو وَالضحّاكَ سِيَرَا * فقد جَاوزتُمَا خَمرَ الطريقِ
(O ʿAmr, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, travel on, for you two have passed the cover of the road.)
al-khamar: whatever conceals you, of trees and other things. (It is permissible) for (الضحّاك) to be accusative or nominative. Another said:
* يا طلحةُ الكاملُ وابن الكَامل *
(O Ṭalḥa, the perfect one and son of the perfect one.)
The naʿt (adjective) runs on the vocative word just as the conjoined does: it is made accusative or nominative. Do you not see that you say إن أخاكَ قائِم وزيد (your brother is standing, and Zayd) and إن أخاك قائم [و] زيدا, so the conjoined after the predicate with إنّ is treated like the naʿt after the predicate?
His saying: ﴿وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ ٱلْحَدِيدَ﴾: iron was made to flow for him, so he would work it as he wished, as one works clay.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿أَنِ ٱعْمَلْ سَابِغَاتٍ﴾: coats of mail; ﴿وَقَدِّرْ فِي ٱلسَّرْدِ﴾: He says: do not make the rivet of the coat of mail thin, so that it is loose, nor thick, so that it breaks the rings.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلِسُلَيْمَانَ ٱلرِّيحَ﴾ is accusative on [the meaning]: and We subjected the wind to Solomon. It is accusative in [Sūrat] al-Anbiyāʾ: ﴿وَلِسُلَيْمَانَ ٱلرِّيحَ عاصِفَةً﴾; He implied "and We subjected" — and Allah knows best. ʿĀṣim — as far as I know — read it nominative (وَلِسُلَيْمَانَ ٱلرِّيحُ), since the subjecting does not appear overtly. One of the Arabs recited to me:
ورأيتُم لمُجَاشعٍ نَعَماً * وبنى أبيه جَامِلٌ رُغُب
(You saw that Mujāshiʿ has livestock, and his father's sons a great, greedy herd of camels.)
He means: and you saw that his father's sons have …; since the verb did not appear, it was made nominative through the lām.
His saying: ﴿غُدُوُّهَا شَهْرٌ وَرَوَاحُهَا شَهْرٌ﴾: He says: its morning journey until midday was a month's travel, and its evening journey likewise.
His saying: ﴿وَأَسَلْنَا لَهُ عَيْنَ ٱلْقِطْرِ﴾ is like ﴿وألَنَّا لَهُ الحَدِيدَ﴾. Al-qiṭr: copper.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ مَا يَشَآءُ مِن مَّحَارِيبَ وَتَمَاثِيلَ﴾: it is mentioned that these were images of the angels and the prophets, which were depicted in the places of worship so that people would see them and increase in worship. Al-maḥārīb: places of worship.
His saying: ﴿وَجِفَانٍ﴾: large bowls; (كالجَوابِ): [like] the troughs for camels; (وَقُدُورٍ رَّاسِيَاتٍ): He says: huge, not taken down from their places.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿تَأْكُلُ مِنسَأَتَهُ﴾: ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash gave it a hamza. It is the large staff that a herdsman carries; taken from نسأت البعير: I drove the camel on to increase its pace; as one says نسأت اللبَن when you pour water onto the milk, and that is al-nasīʾ; and نُسِئت المرأَة when a woman has become pregnant; and نَسَأَ اللهُ فى / 152 a [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] أجلك, i.e. may Allah extend it. The people of the Ḥijāz did not give it a hamza, nor did al-Ḥasan.
Perhaps they intended the dialect of Quraysh, for they drop the hamza. Abū Jaʿfar al-Ruʾāsī claimed to me that he asked Abū ʿAmr about it, (مِنْسَاتَهُ) without hamza, and Abū ʿAmr said: because I do not know it, I dropped its hamza. Had it come in recitation as مِن ساتِهِ, you would make (سَاة) one word and put it in the genitive with مِن. Al-Farrāʾ said: likewise Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: it eats from his staff. The Arabs call the tip of the bow al-siya, so it could be from that; it may take fatḥa or kasra — meaning on the sīn — as one says إِنّ به لضِعَةً and ضَعَة (he has lowliness), and قِحَة and قَحَة, from al-waqāḥa (impudence). But no one we know of has read it so.
His saying: ﴿دَابَّةُ الأَرْضِ﴾: the termite (al-araḍa).
His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّا خَرَّ﴾ — Solomon. According to what is mentioned, [the termite] ate the staff, and he fell. People used to think that the devils knew a secret between two people; when he fell, the matter of the jinn became clear to humankind: that they do not know the unseen, and had they known it they would not have gone on working before him while he was dead. (أَنْ) is in the position of a nominative: ﴿تبيَّن﴾ أن لو كانوا ("it became clear that, had they …"). It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: humankind made the jinn clear [to themselves]; the meaning is then: humankind discerned the matter of the jinn, because when the matter of the jinn became clear to humankind, humankind discerned it; and (أَنْ) is then in the position of an accusative through تبيَّنت. If a reader were to read تبّينتِ الجنّ أن لو كانوا, making the verb belong to humankind and implying them in their verb, he would make الجنّ accusative by the verb of humankind, and (أن) would be repeated [as a badal (substitute)] for الجنّ, so you make it accusative. [Translator's note: the source leaves the conditional without an explicit apodosis such as "it would be correct".]

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ كَانَ لِسَبَإٍ فِي مَسْكَنِهِمْ﴾ was read by Yaḥyā as (فى مَسْكَنِهِمْ), and it is an eloquent Yemeni dialectal form. Ḥamza read (مَسْكِنِهِمْ), and the reading of the general readership is (مَسَاكِنِهِمْ), meaning their dwellings. All are correct. Al-Farrāʾ reads with the reading of Yaḥyā.
His saying: ﴿آيَةٌ جَنَّتَانِ عَن يَمِينٍ وَشِمَالٍ﴾: the meaning is: on their right hands and their left hands. "The two gardens" is nominative because it is an explanation (tafsīr) of the sign. Had one of the two words been accusative through كان, it would have been correct.
His saying: ﴿وَٱشْكُرُواْ لَهُ﴾: the speech is cut off here. ﴿بَلْدَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ﴾: this is a good land, not salt-marsh.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿سَيْلَ ٱلْعَرِمِ﴾: there was a dam that held back the water, with three sluice-gates in it. They would irrigate from that water from the first gate, then the second, then the last, and it would not run out before the water returned in the following year. They were the most comfortable of peoples in their living. When they turned away and denied the messengers, Allah broke the dam upon them, so it flooded their land, and the sand buried their houses, and they were torn utterly apart, until they became a proverb among the Arabs. The Arabs say: تفرقوا أيادِى سَبَا and أيدى سَبَاً (they scattered like the hands of Sabaʾ). The poet said:
عيناً ترى النَّاس إليها نَيْسَبا * من صَادرٍ وواردٍ أيدى سَبَا
(A spring to which you see the people making a beaten track, those leaving and those arriving, scattered like the hands of Sabaʾ.)
They drop its hamza because of how often it runs on their tongues, and some treat سَبا as declinable (yujrūn) and some do not. Whoever does not treat it as declinable takes it to mean the land [Translator's note: the source has البدلة, apparently for البلدة, "the land"]. Whoever treats it as declinable makes Sabaʾ a man or a mountain, and gives it a hamza. In recitation it is mostly with hamza; I know of no one who dropped its hamza. [Someone] recited to me:
الواردونَ وتيم فى ذرى سَبَأ * قد عَضَّ أعناقَهم جِلْدُ الجواميس
(Those who come down to water, and Taym, in the shelter of Sabaʾ — buffalo hide has bitten into their necks.)
His saying ﴿ذَوَاتَيْ أُكُلٍ﴾: al-ukul is pronounced heavy [with two ḍammas]; some of the people of the Ḥijāz pronounced it light. It is read both with annexation and without / 152 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] annexation. As for al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, they pronounced it heavy and did not annex, so they gave it nunation. In the exegesis they mentioned that it is al-barīr, the fruit of the arāk tree. As for al-athl, it is the well-known tree, similar to the tamarisk, except that it is greater in height.
His saying: ﴿وَشَيْءٍ مِّن سِدْرٍ قَلِيلٍ﴾: al-Farrāʾ said: they mentioned that it is al-samur (acacia); its singular is samura.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهَلْ نُجَٰزِيۤ إِلاَّ ٱلْكَفُورَ﴾: so Yaḥyā read it, and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān too. The general readership: (وهَلْ يُجَازَى إلاَّ الكُفُورُ).
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَيْنَاهُمْ﴾: the position of (ذَلِكَ) is accusative through ﴿جَزَيناهم﴾.
Someone may say: how is it that He singled out the ungrateful unbeliever for requital, when requital is for the unbeliever, the Muslim and everyone? It is said: جازيناه is equivalent to كافأناه (We paid him back in kind): the evil deed of the unbeliever with its like. As for the believer, he is rewarded (yujzā), because he is given more and favoured; he is not [merely] paid back (yujāzā). جازيت is also said in the sense of جَزَيت, but the meaning in the clearest speech is as I have described to you; do you not see that He said ﴿ذَلِكَ جَزَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ and did not say ﴿جازيناهم﴾? I have heard جازيت in the sense of جَزيت, and it is like عاقبت and عقَبت, the action being from you alone. And (its pattern — he means —) fāʿaltu is [properly] for your doing and being done to [i.e. mutual action].

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَدَّرْنَا فِيهَا ٱلسَّيْرَ﴾: the distance from one town to the next was made half a day; that is His measuring of the journey.

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿رَبَّنَا بَاعِدْ بَيْنَ أَسْفَارِنَا﴾ is the reading of the general readership. It is also read as a statement: ﴿رَبُّنَا بَعّدَ بَيْنَ أَسْفَارِنا﴾ ("our Lord has made far apart …") and ﴿بَاعَدَ﴾; and it is read as a supplication: ﴿رَبَّنَا بَعِّدْ﴾; and it is read ﴿رَبَّنا بَعُدَ بَيْن أسفارِنا﴾, in which (بَيْنَ) is in the position of a nominative while being accusative [in form]. Whoever makes it nominative treats it like His saying ﴿لقد تقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُ﴾: you make الظن accusative because the confirming falls on it.
